response.title: Maghariba Quarter
response.summary: The historic Maghariba Quarter stood in the south-eastern Old City beside Bab al-Maghariba and al-Buraq Wall.
response.narrative:
The historic Maghariba Quarter stood in the south-eastern Old City beside Bab al-Maghariba and al-Buraq Wall. It was a residential and endowed community associated with people from the Maghreb.

Ayyubid era (late 12th century CE): A charitable endowment is associated with accommodating Maghrebi pilgrims and residents in this area.
Ottoman era (1517-1917 CE): The quarter continued as a residential and religious urban community.
June 1967: Most of the quarter's buildings were demolished and its residents displaced; the physical urban fabric was largely erased.

Main landmarks:
- Bab al-Maghariba.
- Al-Buraq Wall.
- Site of the historic Maghariba Quarter.

A few facts:
- The name refers to the Maghrebi communities connected to the quarter.
- The surviving urban setting differs radically from that before June 1967.
uncertainty_notes: Gaps the AI must not fill: a complete property list, precise demolition chronology for every building and unverified family accounts.
